context:
Goal: a test run that stops partway never reads as passed.
Problem (rule): bin/verdict (the tool that reads a test run and prints one word) has only PASS, SKIP and FAIL, so a log whose stream stopped early has no honest word, and adding a word changes what every reader handles.
Based on (read): the consultant's read of bin/verdict line 99, which passes a log whose stream stopped early, and lines 123 to 128, where an exit code 0 with no test count reads PASS (not re-read by triage).
Departs from: main — verdict has three words and a cut stream can read PASS — a cut stream stops reading PASS.
Waiting on: nothing is stopped; the consultant builds step verdict-cut-stream on your answer.

options.gain: No new word; every reader already handles FAIL.
options.how: A cut stream prints FAIL and the line says it was cut.
options.label: Print FAIL with the word "cut" in the line (recommended)
options.lose: A cut looks like a test failure until someone reads the line.

options.how: bin/verdict prints UNKNOWN for a cut stream.
options.label: Add a new word, UNKNOWN, for a cut stream
options.lose: Every reader of the verdict must learn the new word.
